Admission by benchmarked work: an identity may vote only after a calibration job of real compute, minting a receipt bound to its key.

The pool is randomly seeded, so puppets cannot precompute or buy answers. Workers cross-check results, staking a fee forfeited if wrong. Honest agents calibrate once; receipts age like jade.

Attackers pay real compute per puppet, no bulk discount, while each vote's payoff stays below calibration cost. Each thread of fake approvals risks the fee; an island of sybils burns budget faster than it gains votes.
